A synchronize before any baseline is a misuse, like commit/reset.
delivered_behavior.store_reading: ConsumptionStore.periodSessions(): the period's own records — every harness's, in the document's order.
delivered_behavior.runtime: ModelCostRuntime.synchronize({feedback?}): a period change runs the existing periodSwitched() discard (closed generation's accumulation, Round boundaries and Session spans go with it), a same-generation document that really changed is announced, an identical document redraws nothing, each baseline fault is stated once per reason (and again after a successful read), and after the instance's own cleanup the answer is `closed` with no read at all (no effect after disposal).
delivered_behavior.display: the accrued line now reads periodSessions(), so the period's total and segments are the whole shared document's; the session tree, identities and version chain stay harness-scoped. Docs updated in presentation/display.ts and GLOSSARY.md (new term Read-only synchronization；Accrued bar cross-harness).
delivered_behavior.test_support: store-child extended with harness / syncs / instrumented / ready+go rendezvous and fs call counts (reads, publishes, locks) for its own document; new shared tests/model-cost/support/store-child-runner.ts; scripts/support/efficiency-baseline-fs-instrument.ts gains a namespaceInstrumented() self-check export used to refuse a demanded count from an uninstrumented process.

coverage.P32: S3 real independent processes: a 4-process batch over one document (saved×2 / conflict / stale-version) where each process's own instrument shows publishes = 1 for an accepted record and 0 for a refused one, reads = 2, and the file holds exactly the accepted records (refusals not retried, failures not claimed as saved). A win32 injection (a handle held open on the document) makes the publication fail: reported {kind:'failed', failure:'io'}, publishes = 0, file byte-identical, and the next new process publishes normally with no lock/staging leftover. In-process mixed batch of 4 commits with per-record outcomes. Deterministic in-flight interleaving via the ready/go rendezvous (sync case) and startAt (batch case).
coverage.P33_and_P57_refresh_item: S3 real processes: the syncing process reports {adopted, periodChanged:false, changed:true}, heldSessions includes the other process's records, fsOperations = {reads:2, publishes:0, locks:0} and the file is byte-for-byte what the other writer published. S2 bound runtime: the adopted records appear in view.own/identity and in the detail reading (target current = 3 saved + 1 in flight; tree = 6 including the adopted descendant) while the uncommitted request stays in memory and the file is untouched; an external period switch is taken on as the period, discards the closed generation's accumulation/spans and the following round_end writes nothing; a second synchronization of the same document changes nothing and produces 0 subscriber notifications; the notice cannot make an unsaved record appear.
coverage.P34: initialization: unreadable target, not-JSON, other schema and legacy documents → unusable + pause + notice naming the file + file kept + no repair. runtime: a corrupt document pauses, is stated once, and a second synchronization (target then a directory) proves the file is not read again; an unreadable target is reported with the baseline standing and the Round's next commit then lands normally. A paused instance still makes a real provider query (a deepseek request past the success TTL produces an actual balance request on the substituted transport, address per the approved rule). A normal next initialization rebuilds the baseline (existing + new cases).
coverage.P38: S2 display: a two-harness literal document yields accrued() = {totalCny: 0.875, sessionCostsCny: [0.5, 0.25, 0.125]} while the target's own tree stays harness-scoped; a session's uncommitted request is neither added nor double counted (0.5 before the save, one share after). S3 real processes: the same id in two harnesses and a per-harness + period reading (heldSessions = this harness's one record, periodSessions = both partitions).
coverage.P39: S3 + store: the same session id under two harnesses keeps its own direct parent, version and consumption; all three commits save; a far lower version in one partition is not refused by the other's higher one; the other partition's record is field-for-field what its own process left.

every invariant held; read-only-refresh sequence unchanged at 0 file operations and 0 requests, confirming the period-source change added no I/O to the read path; the store-child instrumented runs measured the new adoption at 1 read, 0 locks, 0 publishes (for ticket 22's comparison)

fault_injection_evidence: A synchronize no longer adopting → 4 cases fail (store + runtime P33)
B synchronize re-publishing the document it adopted → exactly the real-process call-count case fails; the in-process byte comparisons do not, which is why P57 requires counts rather than values

delivered_behavior.follow_read_at_use_point: A `follow` field's subagent reads the Owner's current value: this process's own cell first (in-process direct read, no access opened), otherwise the value the Owner's framework local-access states; declared default while it is not reached. One read rule drives all three public consumptions (injected prompt at run initiation, marker area, capability handed to a handler).
delivered_behavior.degradation: The read never waits for another process; the default answer writes nothing back to the Owner, records nothing in the reader's own medium and is not presented as a read of the Owner's value; the same read returns the Owner's real value once the access is back.
delivered_behavior.recovery: Per-read: concurrent reads of one target merge into one attempt; a failed attempt spaces the next (baseMs×2^(n-1), capped at maxMs); a connected access is never polled (changes are pushed); an ended access is spent and never reused, the read after the spacing opens a fresh one; `StateStore.dispose()` releases every access and stops following for good (pi adapter releases on session_shutdown quit/reload).
delivered_behavior.observation_authority: A delivery whose session is not its own Owner hands out a read-only handle (reads via the field's inheritance rule, every write and notice dropped; same for a handle used after the delivery and for one retained from an owner session_end).
delivered_behavior.followed_seat_rendering: A store that has read an Owner also answers that seat, and the run initiation re-renders the area from the current value, so a line added/removed by the other process does not stay stale.
delivered_behavior.consumer_migration: extensions/codebase-tools/harnesses/pi.ts now states its childEntry (without it the only `follow` consumer was unreachable on pi; ticket 06 recorded this as this ticket's/consumer's wiring). criteria_evidence.P16 (S1): 6 reads in one turn merge into 1 open and all answer the default; after landing they are the Owner's value; an ended access is released (dispose count 1) and the next read reopens and reads the new value with no replayed delivery; spacing asserted exactly as attempts at [0,25,75,135,195,255] ms for {waitMs:20,baseMs:20,maxMs:60} (doubling would place the 6th at 620ms); 200 virtual-clock reads on a healthy access add no open and issue no request; after dispose, 600s of virtual time adds none.

criteria_evidence.P17 (S1): One binding declares owner- and session-scoped groups; on the child's own delivery the session-side capability read observes the Owner's value but its write(false) against the Owner's true and its notify produce no persist record, no marker rendering, no feedback, no cell in this process, and the Owner's own value stays true; the retained child handle behaves the same after the delivery; a child-side command records nothing while the Owner's own command persists {enabled:false} and notifies; a handle retained from the owner session_end is inert from birth.
